description:
Cross-platform conformance vectors for Gemini 3.5 Transcribe Live WebSocket frames (models/gemini-3.5-transcribe-live over BidiGenerateContent). Source of truth: shared-core-rs/crates/hw-net/src/providers/gemini_transcribe.rs, consumed by shared-core-rs/crates/hw-net/tests/live_frame_vectors.rs. The Rust frame builders are deliberately NOT exposed over UniFFI (no platform streaming strategy builds frames across FFI, and per-chunk audio marshalling would add a hot-path copy), so these vectors are how the native streaming strategies on macOS, Windows and Linux are held to the same wire shape. Client-to-server frames only; `expect` is the exact JSON object the client must send, compared structurally (key order is irrelevant).

THE TRAP THIS PINS: the live transcription config lives at `setup.input_audio_transcription`. The pre-recorded location (`setup.generation_config.transcription_config`, which is correct for POST /v1beta/interactions) makes the server close the socket with code 1007. The two models take the same config object at two different paths.

SECOND TRAP, inherited from the pre-recorded path: `custom_vocabulary` is rejected with HTTP 400 / a socket error when sent alongside `diarization_mode` ("custom_vocabulary is incompatible with diarization.") or `timestamp_granularities` ("custom_vocabulary is incompatible with timestamps."). HyperWhisper is a dictation app, so vocabulary wins and the other two are never sent.

audioFormat.note: Audio frame `data` is standard base64 (padded, non-URL-safe, no line breaks) of the raw PCM bytes.

serverMessages.name: one-frame-carrying-both-decodes-as-the-final
serverMessages.note: FINAL WINS. A single serverContent frame may carry inputTranscription AND interimInputTranscription. Every decoder must check the final FIRST: checking the interim first emits only the preview and drops the committed segment, so the user's text ends at the last hypothesis. Key order in this frame is deliberately interim-then-final so a decoder that walks the object in wire order gets it wrong.
